title: 4D analysis of lip competence in children and adolescents
summary:
The competence of the lip closure (competent, potentially competent, incompetent) plays an important role in the context of orthodontic / speech therapy. Incompetent lip closure not only increases the risk of anterior tooth trauma with the risk of losing an upper anterior tooth in childhood, but is also often associated with mouth breathing, which increases the risk of caries and gingivitis. To what extent, however, incompetent lip closure influences the quality of life or how often it is associated with teasing has not yet been clarified.
It is still unclear whether the oral motor skills of patients with competent and incompetent lip closure differ and whether this is objectively measurable reflected in the lip strength and lip movement.
The aim of this prospective, single-center study is to compare the oral health-related quality of life, the risk of teasing, lip movement and lip strength of patients with competent and incompetent lip closure as well as the longitudinal comparison of these variables in patients with incompetent lip closure in the course of a regular orthodontic / speech therapy. For this purpose, 60 patients (incompetent lip closure: n = 30; competent lip closure: n = 30) are initially recruited. The oral health-related quality of life, teasing, lip movement and lip closing force are analyzed.
The data is collected for patients with competent lip closure  before therapy (T0). Patients with incompetent lip closure are investigated three times: T0 = before the start of therapy, T1 = during the course of therapy, T2 = after therapy has been completed. The choice of orthodontic / speech therapy is made by the treating orthodontist / speech therapist regardless of the study.
The results of the planned examination will improve our understanding of the interaction between quality of life, lip movement and function. They will help us to objectively evaluate the success of orthodontic / speech therapy in the future.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
mixed dentition, knowledge in German Language C2 in the Common European Framework of Reference
Exclusion criteria:
- craniofacial syndromes or cleft lip ad/or palate
- impaired facial motion
- beard
- missing informed consent
